chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: حَمْدَوَيْه، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْر، عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَمْرَانَ، عَنِ الْوَلِيدِ بْنِ صَبِيحٍ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from al-Walid ibn Sabih who said:

chunks.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ فَاسْتَقْبَلَنِي زُرَارَةُ خَارِجًا مِنْ عِنْدِهِ، فَقَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: يَا وَلِيدُ أَمَا تَعْجَبُ مِنْ زُرَارَةَ؟ يَسْأَلُنِي عَنْ أَعْمَالِ هَؤُلَاءِ، أَيُّ شَيْءٍ كَانَ يُرِيدُ؟ أَيُرِيدُ أَنْ أَقُولَ لَهُ لَا فَيَرْوِيَ ذَلِكَ عَنِّي؟ ثُمَّ قَالَ: يَا وَلِيدُ مَتَى كَانَتِ الشِّيعَةُ تَسْأَلُ عَنْ أَعْمَالِهِمْ؟ إِنَّمَا كَانَتِ الشِّيعَةُ تَقُولُ: مَنْ أَكَلَ مِنْ طَعَامِهِمْ وَشَرِبَ مِنْ شَرَابِهِمْ وَاسْتَظَلَّ بِظِلِّهِمْ، مَتَى كَانَتِ الشِّيعَةُ تَسْأَلُ عَنْ مِثْلِ هَذَا!

translations.en: I entered to meet Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) and found Zurara exiting from his presence. Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: O Walid, do you not wonder at Zurara? He asks me about the works/actions of these [people], what did he want? Did he want me to say 'No' so that he can narrate that from me? Then he said again: O Walid, when did the Shia ever ask about their works? Rather, the Shia used to say: whoever ate from their food, drank from their drink, and shaded himself in their shade [i.e., lived comfortably with them], when did the Shia ever ask about such [detailed rulings]!

en.summary: In this narration from Rijal al-Kashshi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) gently chides Zurara for his meticulousness in deriving specific legal rulings (fiqh) regarding interactions with the Umayyad elite, contrasting it with the earlier era of 'taqiyya' where Shia were content with basic social integration without detailed scrutiny. This highlights the historical transition in Shia jurisprudence from a period of political suppression and general caution to one of active legal elaboration and scholarly precision. The Imam’s remark underscores the evolution of Shia identity from passive survival to active jurisprudential engagement.
en.seo_question: What does the Imam mean when he asks 'When did the Shia ask about their works?' in this hadith?

key_terms.زُرَارَة: Zurara ibn A'yan, a prominent companion and narrator known for detailed fiqh questions
key_terms.أَعْمَالِ هَؤُلَاءِ: The works/actions of these [people/rulers], referring to dealings with the Umayyads
key_terms.الشِّيعَة: The Shia, referring to the followers of the Imams
key_terms.يَرْوِيَ ذَلِكَ عَنِّي: Narrate that from me, implying attributing a specific legal ruling to the Imam's authority
